articles.title: Who was Noah Woods? 3-year-old non-verbal Suffolk boy with partial hearing loss remembered by father as ‘the sweetest and most innocent little boy’ after body found in pond
articles.summary: UK News: Three-year-old Noah Woods, whose disappearance sparked a large-scale search involving emergency services, police officers and members of the public ac.
articles.body: Three-year-old Noah Woods, whose disappearance sparked a large-scale search involving emergency services, police officers and members of the public across Suffolk, has been remembered by his grieving father as “the sweetest and most innocent little boy” after his body was found in a pond.Noah’s father, Rhys Woods, confirmed the heartbreaking news in a tribute shared after a child’s body was recovered from Decoy Pond in Brantham, Suffolk, on September 16, a day after the toddler went missing.“As I’m sure you have all seen, the body that was found in Decoy pond is our little Noah. There are no words to describe the pain of this loss, we are all absolutely heartbroken,” Rhys wrote. “Noah was the sweetest and most innocent little boy, with nothing but love to give, and we are going to miss him so very much.”Who was Noah Woods?Noah was a three-year-old boy from Brantham, Suffolk, whose disappearance prompted an extensive search involving emergency services and members of the local community.According to Suffolk Constabulary, Noah disappeared on the afternoon of Tuesday, September 15, while visiting a playground on Merriam Close with a relative. He reportedly ran down an alleyway near the playground towards a new housing development.At the time he went missing, Noah was wearing a Bluey T-shirt.Police said Noah was non-verbal and had partial hearing loss. He was also undergoing an assessment for autism. Authorities highlighted these vulnerabilities during the search, explaining that Noah would not respond to his name.Huge search launched for missing toddlerFollowing Noah’s disappearance, a large number of emergency personnel, specialist teams and local residents joined the search.Suffolk Constabulary said officers and staff were deployed in numerous roles to search for the toddler and support his family.Superintendent Tom Pearse said the force had been “overwhelmed by the outpouring of public support,” adding that people had been “putting on their boots and helping us search.”The search involved multiple agencies and organisations, including Suffolk and Norfolk police, the Metropolitan Police, HM Coastguard, Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service, ambulance services and private K-9 units.Members of the local community also opened facilities and provided support as the search continued.Noah’s father thanks everyone who searched for his sonAfter the recovery of the child’s body, Rhys thanked the people who had helped search for Noah, including those who travelled from outside the immediate area.“It seems he has made an impact across the whole nation,” Rhys wrote. “You have all taken Noah into your own hearts, with all the overwhelming help, we were all just trying to bring him home to us safe and sound.”He specifically thanked emergency services, local businesses, community organisations and volunteers who gave their time to help find his son.Among those named in his tribute were Suffolk and Norfolk police, the Metropolitan Police, HM Coastguard, Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service, ambulance services, RTT Catering, Brantham Leisure Centre, Brantham Village Hall, local businesses, St Michael’s Church and private K-9 units.Rhys also thanked people who had put aside their own commitments to join the search.“The compassion shown by all of you will never be forgotten by us, and brought us comfort and strength at the darkest time of our lives,” he wrote.Family had hoped Noah would be found safeRhys said the family continued to hope that Noah would be found alive throughout the search.“This was the most heartbreaking outcome for us,” he wrote. “We were just hoping that he would be hiding somewhere obvious where someone could find him, that’s what we kept telling ourselves the whole time.”Police and dive teams continued searching the area before a child’s body was recovered from Decoy Pond on Wednesday afternoon.While formal identification was initially pending, authorities said Noah’s family had been notified.‘You will be loved forever’In his final message, Rhys spoke on behalf of Noah’s mother and younger brother, promising that the three-year-old would never be forgotten.“Noah, you will be loved forever, you will never be forgotten and we miss you so so much,” he wrote.“It has been a privilege to be your parents and be able to have packed so much love in the short 3 years you were with us.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: UK needs 'credible path' on defence spending, says Nato chief Rutte
articles.summary: Mark Rutte tells the BBC that UK ministers accept the need to make yearly steps to up spending.
articles.body:
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said he is confident the UK government understands the need for a "credible path" to increase defence spending.

The alliance's secretary general told the BBC he was "absolutely confident" in the UK's commitment to hit a Nato-wide spending target of 3.5% of GDP by 2035.

Speaking after meetings in London, he said British ministers accepted the need to make yearly steps towards hitting the target.

But he accepted that the exact "pathway" towards the goal would not be set out until next year.

Andy Burnham has followed predecessor Sir Keir Starmer in committing to reach Nato's 3.5% spending target by 2035, up from an estimated 2.6% this year.

He has said date for reaching a planned 3% interim target will come next spring, when the long-term budgets of government departments are due to be set.

But he has faced pressure to immediately commit to reaching the milestone by the end of the decade. His chancellor and ex-defence secretary John Healey has previously argued this would show Britain was serious about the Nato goal.

Former Dutch PM Rutte has been encouraging members of the alliance not to pencil in large spending increases shortly before the deadline.

Speaking to BBC political editor Chris Mason after meeting Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband in London, Rutte said he was confident British ministers understood the 2035 target could not be met "in one go in 2034".

"I am absolutely confident that when it comes to the 3.5[%] they are there," he said.

"I am absolutely confident that when it comes to the yearly increments, they totally take it and accept it, that they have to be there.

"There has to be a credible path. What that credible path exactly will be, we will see with the spending review next year," he added.

Rutte also said that defence spending should be separated out from the issue of welfare, adding that economic growth was the key to ensuring military commitments could be met alongside spending in other areas.

The Conservatives have been pushing for hikes in defence spending to be funded through cuts to benefits, and have criticised Burnham for saying last week that national security "can't come at the expense of social security".

Rutte added: "I don't know all the details of the UK economy, I think this is something this government is now navigating," he added.

"But I would say these are two separate issues."

"One is, indeed, spending on defence, but the other is of course making sure that the economy is growing enough, so you can distribute the success of a growing economy amongst various income groups, various issues in the Budget, for example welfare and healthcare and the pensions."

"You have to do it all, and if you want to do it successfully, you need economic growth," he added.

"Of course there are issues. I've been prime minister myself for 14 years. You have to take tough decisions, and it's not always easy."

Elsewhere in his interview, Rutte said recent Russian military activity in western Ukraine which saw Poland close two of its airports on Thursday showed Vladimir Putin was "increasingly desperate" over his prospects for the war.

Asked about the possibility of a Russian attack that could demand a Nato response, he replied: "If you are willing to sacrifice 1.2 million of your own people in this crazy unprovoked fight, let's not be naïve about what Putin could do."

He also said there would be discussions among Nato allies over how to respond to the situation in the Red Sea, where Iran-aligned Houthis recently seized control of parts of Yemen's coast along the important shipping route.

Saudi Arabia has relied on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.

"I would not be surprised if some phone calls were taking place between European allies, 'hey, how are we going to deal with this?'" he added.

"Let's see what happens, and if Nato can help, we will always be helpful".

articles.title: Ukrainian guilty of vandalism at mosques linked to Russian network behind Starmer arson attack
articles.summary: Illia Bilyk, a 21-year-old Ukrainian man, has pleaded guilty to targeting five locations in east London.
articles.body:
A Ukrainian man has pleaded guilty to spraying abusive graffiti on mosques in east London, in a case linked to the Russian state network behind arson attacks against the former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer.

Illia Bilyk, 21, entered guilty pleas at Thames Magistrates' Court to five counts of racially and religiously aggravated criminal damage.

Bilyk sprayed graffiti on the Stratford Islamic Association, Al-Birr Mosque and Leyton Jamia Masjid on 23 January 2025. Two days later he targeted Noor Ul Islam Primary School and the Islamic Shariah Council.

The BBC has learned that Bilyk told police he was recruited into spraying the graffiti by a Russian speaker after being approached on the messaging app Telegram.

Bilyk said the Russian speaker told him where to target and paid him afterwards.

In June this year two Ukrainians - Roman Lavrynovych and Stanislav Carpiuc - were jailed for conspiring to carry out arson attacks targeting a property and a car connected to prime minister Sir Keir Starmer.

An investigation by the BBC and Hope not Hate revealed that Russia was behind the arson attacks and had also generated Islamophobic vandalism throughout London, including on the east London venues which Biluyk has now admitted vandalising.

Lavrynovych, who personally started the fires targeting Sir Keir's property, also admitted spraying Islamophobic graffiti on an Islamic building in south London.

He was recruited on Telegram and offered money by an anonymous handler, known by the initials EL, for the graffiti and the arson attacks.

EL was a Russian operative who organised a widespread sabotage and provocation campaign remotely through social media and Telegram.

EL was centrally involved in running a fake far-right group called Direct Action UK, which was created by Russian operatives to provoke acts of vandalism on British streets, including the graffiti attacks on mosques.

After Bilyk sprayed his abusive graffiti in east London in January 2025, images of the attacks were shared in a Direct Action Telegram group.

Hours after two of his attacks, EL posted in a jobs group for Ukrainian people offering money for pictures of buildings in the area.

The BBC investigation named a Russian diplomat, Evgeny Lyukshin, who was part of the Direct Action UK chat group. Lyukshin was trained in "information warfare" by senior Russian spies and his details matched those of EL. He did not respond to the BBC.

Bilyk will be sentenced on 19 October at Stratford Magistrates' Court.

Chief Superintendent Rhona Hunt, from the Met Police, said: "We recognise that these incidents caused significant distress within Muslim communities across east London last year and that they continue to cause concern.

"Anti-Muslim hate crime and Islamophobia have absolutely no place in London. We are committed to tackling hate crime while supporting and reassuring our communities."

articles.title: Charles 'sounded giddily elated' night Diana died, Earl Spencer claims
articles.summary: Buckingham Palace has strongly pushed back against the claims in a new book by the late Princess of Wales's brother.
articles.body:
Earl Spencer, brother of Diana, Princess of Wales, has claimed King Charles "sounded giddily elated" when he called him on the night of her death in 1997.

In a controversial book about her life, he recalled thinking the then-Prince Charles sounded like a "lottery winner" after the news.

Yesterday, Buckingham Palace strongly pushed back against the book, after an initial extract claimed Charles had said of Diana: "We'll forget her soon enough."

A spokesperson said: "While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss."

William and Catherine visit Bute and King opens AI summit as row erupts over Diana book

Palace in war of words with Earl Spencer over claims in Diana book

'Grief can colour memory': Palace responds after Earl Spencer's claim in Diana book

According to excerpts from Earl Spencer's memoir published in the Daily Mail , he remembers being alerted to the car crash on 31 August, 1997, by a phone call from his sister Jane in the middle of the night at his home in Cape Town, South Africa.

During the calls that followed, which confirmed the death, Charles phoned him as he was crossing the landing, he writes.

The book alleges: "Unlike my other callers, who were stunned, barely able to articulate their condolences and offers of help, he sounded giddily elated - like a lottery winner, I remember thinking at the time."

According to Earl Spencer, Charles informed him he had told Princes William and Harry of their mother's death first thing that morning, in their bedrooms at Balmoral.

The royal couple had divorced in August 1996.

Swan Song: Diana, My Sister is due to be published next week and is expected to be highly critical of the Royal Family. BBC News has not seen the book in full.

In the memoir, Earl Spencer writes of his sister's troubled marriage - claiming Charles told her on the eve of their wedding in July 1981 that he was "very happy to marry her, but… not actually in love with her".

Things became "very difficult indeed" in the marriage early on, Earl Spencer writes, adding that he is "sure that both spouses despaired of the other at times".

He now believes his sister had attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and as part of her condition suffered from Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria - describing the latter as an "intense emotional pain in the face of others' rejection or criticism".

In her later years, he writes, Princess Diana considered taking her own life on more than one occasion but love for her sons "stopped her from going further".

articles.title: China moved 64 rare Milu deer to a reserve in 1993 and 1994, but a 1998 flood sent 36 into the wild, where their population topped 500
articles.summary: Rest of World News: The Père David’s deer, or Milu, had disappeared from the wild in China by the early 20th century, making its later return an unusual conservation stor.
articles.body: The Père David’s deer, or Milu, had disappeared from the wild in China by the early 20th century, making its later return an unusual conservation story. In 1993 and 1994, 64 Milu were transferred to the Hubei Shishou Milu National Nature Reserve, an island reserve along the Yangtze River. Then, during a severe flood in May 1998, 36 animals escaped and crossed the swollen river. What followed was an unexpected experiment in natural re-wilding, as the deer found new habitats, bred and gradually established populations beyond the reserve.Why 64 rare Milu were returned to the Chinese reserveThe Milu, scientifically known as Elaphurus davidianus, is native to China and is particularly adapted to wetland environments. The species had once been widely distributed around the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River, but habitat loss, hunting and climate change contributed to its disappearance from the country around the beginning of the 20th century. According to the study titled ‘Stepping-stones and dispersal flow: establishment of a meta-population of Milu (Elaphurus davidianus) through natural re-wilding’ conducted by Institute of Zoology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, China, the reintroduction efforts began with animals brought from England to Beijing Milu Park in 1985. In 1991, Hubei Shishou Milu National Nature Reserve was established on an island in the Yangtze. A total of 64 Milu were subsequently transferred there from Beijing Milu Park during 1993 and 1994.A 1998 flood changed the course of the reintroductionFor several years, the Milu remained within and around the reserve, occasionally attempting short movements into surrounding areas. That changed dramatically in May 1998, when the Yangtze experienced heavy flooding. A herd of 36 Milu escaped from the reserve and swam across the flooded river. Researchers later recorded that the animals could not simply be driven back because they had moved into swampy areas. Instead, the escape became the starting point for a naturally developing population outside the protected reserve. The researchers monitored the animals through regular surveys, recording their movements, numbers, habitats and subsequent dispersal between suitable areas.The escaped deer found ‘stepping stones’ across the landscapeThe escaped Milu did not simply remain in one location. They moved between suitable patches of habitat, using what the researchers described as “stepping stones,” areas that provided food and shelter within a landscape otherwise unsuitable for continuous movement. Some of these places became refuges where the deer stayed and reproduced. Between 1995 and 2012, researchers recorded 122 dispersal events involving the escaped Milu. Most dispersal events occurred in 1998, 2003, 2006 and 2010, while the average dispersal distance was about 14.08 kilometres. More than 91% of recorded movements were shorter than 25 kilometres.The population eventually exceeded 500 via natural re-wildingThe accidental escape ultimately produced a notable example of natural re-wilding. The researchers found that the escaped Milu successfully established populations and reproduced in the wild. By the end of 2009, the number of naturally re-wilded Milu and their descendants had exceeded 500. The population later declined during a disease outbreak in February and March 2010, while by the end of 2012 around 300 wild Milu were scattered across refuge populations on the eastern and southern edges of Dongting Lake. The study concluded that floods and human disturbance helped trigger dispersal, while population density was an important underlying driver.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: US advances $24.3 billion Saudi F-35 deal despite concerns over kingdom's China ties
articles.summary: International News: The US State Department has approved the potential sale of Lockheed Martin’s F-35 Lightning II fighter jets to Saudi Arabia for an estimated $24.3 bil.
articles.body: The US State Department has approved the potential sale of Lockheed Martin’s F-35 Lightning II fighter jets to Saudi Arabia for an estimated $24.3 billion, according to a notice posted online on Thursday.The kingdom has been drawn deeper into the Middle East war as it pursues the advanced aircraft.The proposed sale puts Saudi Arabia closer to acquiring one of the world’s most advanced fighter aircraft after years of seeking the F-35 from Washington.Saudi Arabia has had decades of military cooperation with the US and is the largest buyer of American weapons and defence equipment.The State Department’s approval comes amid heightened scrutiny over Saudi Arabia’s military and security ties with China.US intelligence officials have raised concerns that Beijing could potentially gain access to F-35 technology through espionage in Saudi Arabia or through the kingdom’s military and security partnership with China, The New York Times reported.F-35 deal faces China-related security concernsThe projected sale of approximately $24.3 billion would include 48 military aircraft and 49 engines from Pratt & Whitney, as well as communication gear, spare parts, and additional support items, according to the department.The State Department sent the package to two congressional committees in June for informal approval, as the administration moved the sale into a more advanced stage.A Pentagon Defense Intelligence Agency report circulated among government agencies and congressional offices reportedly raised concerns about Chinese military access to Saudi bases and the kingdom’s use of Chinese telecommunications technology.US intelligence analysts have questioned whether secure facilities could be maintained for the F-35 technology and whether Saudi Arabia would agree to restrict access by Chinese military and intelligence personnel.The report also raised questions about the presence of equipment from Chinese technology companies Huawei and ZTE in telecommunications, router infrastructure and defence installations.The Pentagon is particularly concerned about protecting the F-35’s advanced radar and surveillance technology, the newspaper reported.The US intelligence concerns are not new. Similar issues emerged during the first Trump administration over a proposed F-35 sale to the United Arab Emirates.The Biden administration later ended that sales process after reviewing concerns about the UAE’s expanding military, intelligence and technology links with China, according to The New York Times.Saudi Arabia’s military ties with ChinaSaudi Arabia maintains close military ties with Washington but also has defence cooperation with Beijing.Saudi Arabia buys ballistic missiles from China and that the Chinese military has helped the kingdom develop ballistic missiles, establish production facilities and improve missile operations.The newspaper also reported that Prince Mohammed has sought to strengthen Saudi Arabia’s military capabilities while the kingdom has faced renewed fighting with the Houthis, an Iran-backed group in Yemen.Saudi Arabia has led a coalition fighting the Houthis since 2015. The conflict has intensified again, with the Houthis launching drones and missiles at Saudi targets.Saudi Arabia said on Thursday that debris from an intercepted Houthi drone killed one person and injured two others in Taif province. The Houthis have denied targeting Mecca, after Saudi Arabia said on Wednesday that it had intercepted a drone aimed at the holy city.Israel’s military edge also a considerationThe proposed F-35 sale could also draw scrutiny over Israel’s military advantage in the Middle East.Israel is currently the only country in the region operating F-35 fighter jets. US policymakers have historically sought to preserve Israel’s “qualitative military edge” in the region, a requirement mandated by Congress.Previous US administrations have therefore subjected proposed advanced weapons sales to Arab countries in the region to detailed reviews.Saudi Arabia’s potential acquisition comes alongside broader US-Saudi defence and strategic discussions. The Trump administration has also agreed to help the kingdom develop a civilian nuclear programme, a separate issue that has raised security concerns.The State Department said in its notice that “the proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the military balance in the region.”The State Department’s approval does not itself complete the F-35 sale. The proposed package remains subject to the US arms-sales process and congressional scrutiny.

articles.title: ‘Late night birthday gift to Modi ji’: Congress slams EC over TMC symbol freeze
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Congress on Thursday criticised the Election Commission's interim decision to bar both rival Trinamool Congress (TMC) factions from using t.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress on Thursday criticised the Election Commission's interim decision to bar both rival Trinamool Congress (TMC) factions from using the party's name and reserved election symbol in the upcoming West Bengal Assembly bypolls, with party general secretary KC Venugopal calling it “CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s late night birthday gift to Modi ji”.In a post on X, Venugopal alleged that the decision amounted to an attempt to undermine the faction led by West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee."Freezing the AITC name and symbol - after a blatantly unconstitutional hijack by the BJP - is CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s late night birthday gift to Modi ji.Those who fought against the BJP, under Mamata Banerjee’s leadership, are now being given the red carpet to rebel against her and commit the unconstitutional sin of defection with the ECI’s help.The ECI has one again proven that it is nothing more than a puppet in the hands of the BJP - a tool to destroy democracy bit by bit.They did it in the case of Shiv Sena, NCP, and now AITC - whoever opposes the BJP is dealt a fatal blow and their entire electoral existence is snatched away from them.We condemn this move, and demand that the ECI immediately restore the two leaves symbol to Mamata Banerjee ji."The Congress leader's remarks came shortly after the Election Commission barred both rival TMC factions from using the party name and reserved election symbol for the October 6 West Bengal Assembly bypolls.The bypolls are scheduled in Nandigram and Rejinagar, where factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Ritabrata Banerjee had fielded candidates while staking claim to the TMC identity and its twin-flowers-on-grass symbol.The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions claimed control of the party. The poll panel subsequently sought submissions on organisational control, authorised signatories, party assets, the party name and the election symbol.The EC held separate meetings with representatives of both factions on September 12. The Mamata faction was represented by Derek O'Brien, Kalyan Banerjee, Sagarika Ghose, Saket Gokhale and advocate Abhinav Singh, while the Ritabrata faction was represented by Ritabrata Banerjee, Akhruzzaman, Arup Roy, Chandrima Bhattacharya and Riju Datt.The Mamata faction argued that Banerjee remained the party chairperson and that its national working committee was within its five-year term. The rival faction contended that the party constitution provided for a three-year term, which it said had ended in February 2025.The EC sought final submissions from both factions by 3 pm on September 16, the nomination deadline for the bypolls, and subsequently held another hearing on Thursday.The interim order comes ahead of the October 6 bypolls and while the broader dispute over control of the party remains unresolved.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Wife of US scholar detained in China asks Trump to raise case with Xi during White House meet
articles.summary: US News: A US scholar who was invited to China for an academic event and later detained on national security charges has become the subject of a direct appeal .
articles.body: A US scholar who was invited to China for an academic event and later detained on national security charges has become the subject of a direct appeal to US President Donald Trump ahead of his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.The wife of U Min Zin, a Myanmar politics scholar and head of the Myanmar Institute for Strategic and Policy Studies (ISP-Myanmar), has urged Trump to raise her husband's case with Xi and seek his release when the Chinese president visits Washington next week.Min Zin travelled to the Chinese city of Kunming in June after being invited to attend an academic workshop. He subsequently disappeared from contact and was later detained by Chinese authorities on suspicion of endangering national security, according to his wife, Sylvia Zin.“I’m deeply hopeful that President Trump will raise my husband’s case with President Xi Jinping at the summit next week,” Sylvia Zin told a US congressional hearing on Wednesday.Wife has not spoken to husbandSylvia Zin said she has still not been able to speak directly with her husband and relies on visits by US consular officials for updates about his condition.“Every month, we anxiously await his consular visits because they reassure us that he is alive,” she told lawmakers.She said US officials told her that Min Zin was interrogated for four to six hours a day when he was initially detained and is being held in a small cell where the light remains on around the clock.“I’m trying to be strong for our daughter, but I’m constantly wondering if he’s OK and how to get him back home to us,” she said.Min Zin, 53, is one of two US citizens whom the State Department has designated as “wrongfully detained” in China. The other is US seismologist Youlin Chen, who has been imprisoned in China for nearly two years.The designation allows the cases to be handled by the US Special Envoy for Hostage Affairs, raising their priority within the US government and allowing additional resources to be used in efforts to secure their release.Families seek Trump’s interventionThe cases have gained attention in Washington ahead of Xi's expected visit. Families of Americans detained in China travelled to the US capital this week to press for their release.The son of imprisoned Hong Kong media mogul Jimmy Lai also appeared on Capitol Hill, urging Trump to seek his father's release on humanitarian grounds.Trump had previously raised Lai's case with Xi during his May visit to China. Trump later said Xi had told him that Lai's case would be “a tough one”.The US president has also previously pressed Xi over the detention of Chinese pastor Jin Mingri, who was released two months after Trump's request.A senior White House official told the BBC that resolving the wrongful detention of US citizens “is always a top priority for the President.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
